# Translations

<!-- Generated by scripts/l10n/l10n.py generate. Don't edit: change the tool, scripts/l10n/overrides.tsv, scripts/l10n/machine or scripts/l10n/languages.tsv and run scripts/l10n/update.sh. -->

Greenshot for Mac (Community) reuses the translations of Greenshot for Windows: its language packs (upstream commit `0aedcf04`, vendored in `scripts/l10n/upstream`) are matched with the Mac's English texts. A Mac text whose English is also an upstream text (the same words; an ellipsis, a trailing colon, spaces and capitals don't count) gets that text's translation; a text without an upstream translation in a language gets a machine translation from `scripts/l10n/machine/<lproj>.tsv` ([Machine translations](#machine-translations)), and a text with neither stays English. The packs are GPL, like this app; the translators' credits are in each pack (`about_translation`) and About shows the one of the language in use.

## How it works

- `scripts/l10n/extract.sh` builds the app with the compiler's `-emit-localized-strings` and writes every localizable text (SwiftUI literals, `String(localized:)`) to `scripts/l10n/mac-keys.json`.
- `scripts/l10n/l10n.py generate` matches them with the upstream English (`scripts/l10n/overrides.tsv` maps near matches by hand or rejects a wrong one) and writes `Resources/Localizations/<language>.lproj/Localizable.strings`, the `Upstream.strings` table for texts that are also data (`L10nText.display`) and `LanguagePacks+Generated.swift`. `scripts/l10n/update.sh` runs both steps.
- `scripts/l10n/machine/<lproj>.tsv` holds the machine translations of a language (`English<TAB>translation<TAB>source`, one row per Mac text without an upstream translation in that language). `generate` and `check` use them unless they get `--no-machine`; an upstream translation or an overrides.tsv decision always wins over a row.
- `scripts/build-app.sh` copies the `.lproj` folders and the help pages (`Resources/Help`) into the app and lists the languages in `CFBundleLocalizations`, so macOS offers them in System Settings › General › Language & Region › Applications.
- `scripts/l10n/l10n.py check` (CI) fails when the committed files differ from what `generate` writes.
- New texts in the code: SwiftUI literals need nothing; AppKit and other texts use `String(localized: "…")`. Logs, data, identifiers and recipe/IPC/MCP texts stay English. `scripts/l10n/scan.sh [--summary] <paths>` lists the texts of a file that aren't localizable yet.
- Updating from upstream: `python3 -I scripts/l10n/l10n.py vendor --upstream <checkout>`, then `scripts/l10n/update.sh`, then review `python3 -I scripts/l10n/l10n.py suggest` for new near matches.
- Trying a language in a development build: `scripts/l10n/stage-dev.sh`, then `GreenshotMac --language de-DE` (or `--snapshot <folder> --language ar-SY`).

## Machine translations

24827 translations in 13 languages are machine translations (0 of them reviewed by a person): the Mac's texts that Greenshot's translators haven't translated, because the Mac wrote them or the language pack doesn't have them yet. An AI model made them; `l10n.py` checks their placeholders and Windows wording, nobody checked their language unless the row says reviewed. They are marked:

- in `Localizable.strings` by `/* machine */` above the entry (`/* machine, reviewed */` once a person checked it), and in the Machine column of the table above;
- in the app: About shows "Some texts in this language are machine translations." under the translators' credit (`L10nText.hasMachineTranslations`).

Correcting one: edit its row in `scripts/l10n/machine/<lproj>.tsv` (keep the English of the first column exactly as it is; `\n` is a line break; keep every `%@`, `%lld` …, numbered like `%2$@ … %1$@` to change their order, and write a literal percent sign as `%%` in a text with placeholders), set its source (third column) to `reviewed by <name>`, and run `scripts/l10n/update.sh`. Delete the row to show the English instead. A translation of an upstream text belongs in Greenshot's language pack: once it is vendored, it replaces the machine translation here.

New texts in the code: `python3 -I scripts/l10n/l10n.py untranslated` lists the texts without a translation (`<lproj><TAB>English`); add their rows to the tables with the model or person as the source.

Sources: claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-18 (6 rows), claude-sonnet-5-5 2026-10-18 (25693 rows).
